question.text:
How many paths are there from the lower left corner to the upper right corner, moving only up or to the right ?

Path can not go through any of the dotted lines 

  1. $\begin{pmatrix} 20 \\ 10 \end{pmatrix} - \bigg[ \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 10 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 14 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3  \end{pmatrix} \bigg]$
  2. $\begin{pmatrix} 20 \\ 10 \end{pmatrix} - \bigg[ \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 10 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 14 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3  \end{pmatrix} \bigg]$
  3. $\begin{pmatrix} 20 \\ 10 \end{pmatrix} - \bigg[ \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 10 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 14 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix}  4 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3  \end{pmatrix} \bigg]$
  4. $\begin{pmatrix} 20 \\ 10 \end{pmatrix} - \bigg[ \begin{pmatrix} 10 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 10 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 14 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3  \end{pmatrix} \bigg]$

In how many ways can $2$ RED and $4$ BLUE  ROOKS be placed on an $8-by-8$ board so that no two ROOKS can attack one another?

  1. $8! \times 8!$
  2. $8! \times \frac{8!}{2!4!}$
  3. $8! \times \frac{8!}{2!4!2!2!}$
  4. ${}^8P_4$
How many numbers in $\{1, 2, \ldots,10000\}$ have their digits sum to $7?\:(e.g. 502)$
The number of permutations of $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ in which at least one odd integer is in its natural position is ______
In how many ways can the letters $\{a, b, c, d, e\}$ be placed into $3$ identical boxes such that no box is empty?

In how many ways can $10$ women and $4$ men line up in a straight line so that no two men are consecutive?

  1. $10! \begin{pmatrix} 11 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} 4!$
  2. $10! \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} 4!$
  3. $\frac{14!}{4!}$
  4. $\begin{pmatrix} 11 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} $

$50$ people are to be divided (partitioned) into $5$ teams of $10$ players each. In how many ways can this be done if each team has a different name

  1. $\frac{50!}{10!^5}$
  2. $\frac{50!}{5!^{10}}$
  3. $\frac{\begin{pmatrix}50 \\ 10 \end{pmatrix}}{10!}$
  4. None

A bowl contains $5$ red balls and $7$ silver ones. A woman chooses balls at random without looking at them. How many must she choose, to be sure of having at least $3$ of the same color?

  1. $7$
  2. $11$
  3. $10$
  4. $5$
How many bit strings of length $6$ have more zeroes than ones?

How many license plates with $3$ decimal digits followed by $3$ letters do not contain both the number $0$ and the letter $\text{O}$?

  1. $17047279$
  2. $14074279$
  3. $17074279$
  4. $12436759$
A decimal number is called “increasing” if each digit is greater than the previous one (e.g. $24589$ is one). How many $5$ digit increasing numbers are there?

How many even integers $≥ 4000$ and $< 7000$ have four different digits?

  1. $128$
  2. $728$
  3. $328$
  4. $528$
How many ways are there to seat $10$ people, consisting of $5$ couples, in a row of seats ($10$ seats wide) if all couples are to get adjacent seats?

An integer is called snakelike if its decimal representation $a_1a_2a_3 \dots a_k$ satisfies $a_i < a_{i+1}$ if $i$ is odd and $a_i > a_{i+1}$ if $i$ is even. How many snakelike integers between $1000$ and $9999$ have four distinct digits?

A landscaper is planting a row of $12$ trees including $4$ birch trees and $8$ pine trees. How many ways can this be done without having two birch trees next to each other?

  1. $\frac{16!}{12!4!}$
  2. $\frac{16!}{12!}$
  3. $\frac{16!}{4!}$
  4. $\begin{pmatrix}9 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$

How many solutions does the equation $a+b+c+d+e+f = 2006$ have where $a, b, c, d, e$ and $f$ are all positive integers?

  1. $\begin{pmatrix} 2005 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$
  2. $\begin{pmatrix} 2006 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$
  3. $\begin{pmatrix} 2011 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$
  4. $\begin{pmatrix} 2005 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$
How many bit strings of length $5$ are there, such that every $1$ is followed immediately by a zero?
How many numbers (minimum) must you pick to ensure that at least three of them have the same remainder when divided by $11?$
A pool of available computer programmers has $13$ members–six men and seven women In how many ways can you choose a team of five, with at most three men?
How many ways a set of $5$ elements can be divided into two unordered partitions where each partition gets at least one element?
